visual.detail: Manager must inspect all views for placement, proportions, missing/extra parts and visible intersections
visual.observation: Front: one sphere seated centrally on a drafted disc that flares outward as it rises, with the hoop seen nearly edge-on as a narrow tab above the ball and its two feet meeting the disc top. Top: the disc's rim is concentric with the ball and the hoop crosses the globe as a single upright line through the middle. Iso: the hoop is a narrow band standing over the ball and leaning toward +X, springing from the globe all the way round with no gap and no unsupported air. Nothing is drawn on the sphere -- the surface is one unbroken curve in all three views, which is what a bare globe should look like. Proportion Ø22.02 globe on a Ø33.87 disc reads correctly; no extra or missing bodies, no interpenetration, no floating geometry.
